detail.finding: Looking for an installed copy of the game…
detail.notInstalled: No installed copy found, and that is fine: the decoy does not need one.
detail.noteDone: You can stop it now, the quest should be counted.

running.empty.title: Nothing is running

settings.title: Settings
settings.language.desc: Interface language. New languages are added as files in the locales folder.
settings.defaultTime.desc: How many minutes to keep the process. The default is 16, not 15: Discord quests ask for 15 minutes of play, but Discord needs up to a minute to notice a new game, so exactly 15 falls short.
settings.smartTimer.desc: The countdown starts when Discord has noticed the decoy, not when you start it. To know that, the app reads only the lines about the running game from Discord's local log; nothing is stored or sent anywhere.
settings.autoUpdate.desc: Check GitHub at startup and every 6 hours and download new versions in the background. Installing always waits for your confirmation, and files are verified by their digital signature.
update.uptodate: You are on the latest version
detail.waitingNote: Discord needs up to a minute to notice a game. The countdown starts when it sees the decoy.
detail.assumed: Discord has not confirmed it, the time is counted anyway.
settings.autoStop.desc: The decoy ends by itself when the time is up.
settings.notify.desc: A Windows notification when the time is up.
settings.tray.desc: Decoys keep running while the app is in the tray.
settings.showNoExe.desc: Entries where Discord does not know the process yet (they cannot be started).
settings.dataDir.desc: Where the game list and settings are stored.
settings.dataDir.portable: Portable mode: everything is stored next to decoy.exe.
settings.legal: Decoy does not use your Discord token and does not accept quests for you. Faking a game process may go against Discord's rules, use it at your own risk.
toast.launched: “{name}” started for {n} min. Discord should notice it in about 15 seconds.
toast.timeUp: Time is up, the quest should be counted
toast.refreshUpToDate: The database is already up to date
lab.title: Lab
lab.subtitle: A secret tab: starts many decoys at once.
lab.count.desc: Games are picked at random, ones already running are skipped. Each one runs for {n} min (set in Settings).
lab.warn: Every decoy is a separate process with a window. Too many at once can freeze your computer: each process and window uses memory, and after a few thousand windows Windows may stop creating more. If you close Decoy, all decoys stop.
lab.risk.mid: From about 250 decoys on, Discord itself may slow down: it tracks every running game and reports it to its servers.
lab.risk.high: Danger: when 5,000 decoys were started at once, Discord grew past 10 GB of RAM and crashed every 30 seconds until its local data was reset. Decoy stops everything if Discord's memory jumps, but there is no guarantee.
lab.discordRam: Discord is using {gb} GB of RAM right now.
lab.unlock.desc: Above this limit Discord has broken in practice. Turn it on only if you understand the risk.
guard.tripped: All decoys stopped to protect Discord: it uses {gb} GB of RAM (up {grew} GB). If it is slow, restart it.
lab.estimate: {n} decoys will use roughly {ram} of RAM.
lab.limit: Windows stopped starting new processes after {n}: that is the system limit.
notify.title: Time is up
